correctness.rationale: All message differences reduce to 1,2,3-bit support checks; these are exactly distinct r-bit columns of weight >=3 with no sum triple. The published Davydov--Tombak stability theorem forces affine-hyperplane containment above the explicit \(5\cdot2^{r-4}\) threshold for every \(r\ge5\). Each hyperplane with a normal of weight s loses exactly s+s(r-s) excluded columns, at least r; equality gives s=1 or r. Small r are solved directly. The finite verifier exhausts \(r\le5\) and replayed correctly; no finite-to-infinite inference.

Two particularly relevant 2026 systematicity preprints were accessible as abstracts only; they do not advertise the distance-four joint profile, but a hidden exact special case remains possible.
Older unequal-error-protection coding literature might use a non-obvious equivalent restricted-column formulation.

value.rationale: Determines an exact naturally motivated fixed-overhead design frontier and all optimal encoders, with a sharp exceptional \(r=4\) transition. Distinguishes all r genuinely strict codes from the sole nonstrict distance-four optimizer for every \(r\ge5\). The parity attribute is a natural binary modular-sum statistic, and the full classification is not a routine known-table recomputation.
